mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals sustained monetary accommodation that lowers discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is ≤0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST < 1200) and real personal consumption (RSAFS < 450000) signal weakening consumer demand that triggers negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100.0 indicates slowing economic activity that reduces corporate profit expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and regime is late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1200.0 thousand units signal robust consumer demand for housing, which correlates with rising corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1200.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 240.0 indicates accelerating inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 240.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS > 144000) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.0) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals aggressive interest rate hikes that increase borrowing costs and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and regime is monetary tightening.
